what_source_says: LRQA: white-label USB-charger spy camera, device family 'TUT', PPPP from CS2; 'Recordings and snapshots are uploaded to Aliyun (Alibaba Cloud) OSS buckets'; bucket 'hosted in China' with thousands of folders named after camera IDs and date subfolders of periodic snapshots; 'App to bucket interactions run over cleartext HTTP'; camera upload transport not stated; app not named; no disclosure timeline. Palant: HomeEye app (package shix.homeeye.camera) row lists prefixes 'AYS AYSA TUT', protocol 'JSON (SHIX)'; nothing on cloud uploads. Meari CVE: alert images on Alibaba OSS retrievable without authentication (other vendor). LookCam: video chunks to vendor servers over unencrypted HTTP (other family, not OSS). Ren IMC'19: video experiments had the lowest fraction of encrypted bytes (aggregate, other devices); no Home Eye/SimCam.
difference: No paper on this product or family found. LRQA is a different device (TUT prefix vs AYS here), app unnamed, region/endpoint not given (ours: oss-cn-hongkong), and it reports app-to-bucket cleartext HTTP, not camera-to-bucket. Ours: the camera itself PUTs full photos over port 80 at power-on (3 of 3 power captures, also idle nights), seen passively in a 2021 public capture; LRQA is 2026 active RE. The link CIC device -> LRQA device rests only on Palant putting AYS and TUT in the same app row (shared by 3 apps) = inference.

what_source_says: LRQA: hardcoded Alibaba OSS access keys found in firmware (/usrdata) and in the Android app BuildConfig; app had 'three bucket key pairs hardcoded for three brands', one live; keys give access to everyone's snapshots. Zuo et al. S&P'19: key misuse in 1.6M Android apps for AWS/Azure/Firebase back ends; no Alibaba OSS, no IoT device traffic, no plain-HTTP facet.
difference: LRQA recovered the secret key by reverse engineering (active); ours only sees the key ID (not secret by design) in cleartext, plus per-request signatures. A fixed key ID on one device suggests a device- or fleet-wide key but cannot show it is shared across devices (only one Home Eye unit in CIC) = 未確認. Signed requests over HTTP can be replayed within the provider's time window (not tested; passive only).
